item.title: GIANNO CALDWELL: We marched for every family blue city politicians left behind
item.description: The march drew crowds near where the author's brother was murdered, but Gov. JB Pritzker and Mayor Brandon Johnson never responded to invitations.
item.content:encoded:
This weekend I marched through the streets of Chicago, a few blocks from where my innocent teenage brother Christian was murdered four years ago.

That loss is what led me to found the Caldwell Foundation for Public Safety, driven by one belief: that no family should ever have to go through what mine did. Community members lined the sidewalks and cheered as we passed. That moment told me everything I needed to know about who is truly fighting for these communities and who isn't.

I invited Illinois Governor JB Pritzker and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson to join us. I called their offices. I emailed them. I listed the invitation in my Fox News op-ed. I extended the invitation publicly on national and local television multiple times. They never responded. Not once. Not a word. Not an acknowledgment. Two of the most powerful elected officials in Illinois could not even extend the basic courtesy of a response to the families of murder victims gathering in their own city.

GIANNO CALDWELL: FOUR YEARS AFTER MY BROTHER’S MURDER, I’M MARCHING FOR JUSTICE

Let that settle in. The governor of Illinois and the mayor of Chicago took an oath to serve the people of this state and this city. They had no answer for the mothers who have buried their children. No answer for the fathers who live with a hole in their hearts that never heals. No answer for the communities that have been failed by the same political machine for decades. They chose not to respond. Again and again.

Their silence was loud. And the community noticed.

This is what failed leadership looks like in real time. Chicago was once one of the great economic engines of the Midwest. Today it is a cautionary tale. Ken Griffin, one of the most successful investors in American history, lived in Chicago for more than 30 years before packing up Citadel and 900 employees and moving to Miami. He did not leave quietly. "I had two colleagues who had bullets fly through their cars," Griffin told Fox News. "I had 25 bullet holes in the front of my building where I lived. You can't live in a city awash in violent crime." Illinois has lost a net 1.6 million people to domestic outmigration since 2000, and Chicago's population is at its lowest level in nearly a century. The families who cannot afford to leave are the ones paying the price for every bad policy decision made by the people who were supposed to protect them. And in some cases, they are paying with their lives.

NORTH TEXAS DOMINATES IN POPULATION GROWTH AS BIG BLUE CITIES FAIL TO RECOVER TO PRE-PANDEMIC LEVELS

Nearly 7,000 people have been murdered in Chicago over the last decade. Seven thousand. They are sons and daughters. Brothers and sisters. Friends and neighbors. People who deserved to grow old, to raise families, to build something with their lives. Darren Bailey, the Republican nominee challenging Governor Pritzker, captured the purpose of the march when he said: "People in Chicago shouldn't be living under a death sentence, and that's essentially what's taking place right now. Gianno's brother Christian should be here today, and this summer, and at this school, and he's not." He is right. Christian should be here. So should every victim taken from this city over the last decade. Bob Fioretti, the Republican candidate for Illinois Attorney General, put the current toll in stark terms: "So far in the city of Chicago this year, over 1,000 people have been shot. 220 of them have been killed. Last night alone in our city, there was one killed, six wounded. This is unacceptable."

Among those who spoke at the march was Apostle Anthony Wilson, a man of God and a grieving father who stood before the crowd and shared the story of his daughter Alicia Prince, murdered just two months ago. "No one should have to bury their child before their time," he said, pausing to collect himself before the crowd. Two months. Her family is still in shock, thrust into a reality too many families know all too well. Apostle Wilson's presence embodied everything this march was about. Not politics. Not party. A father demanding that his daughter's life meant something. That it must mean something.

Christian Maxwell, who is running for Congress in Illinois's 1st Congressional District, spoke to the heart of what is at stake for these communities. "Safety is not partisan," she said. "We want to fight for children to be able to ride their bikes and walk to school safely. That is not a hard thing to achieve when leaders are focused on the right outcome."

CHICAGO PASTOR GATHERS HUNDREDS OF MEN TO DECLARE VIOLENCE-FREE ZONE ON SOUTH SIDE

Christine McGovern, who is running for Illinois State Senate in the district where we marched, spoke to something that too many people are afraid to say out loud. "They are so desensitized to what has happened," she said. "We cannot normalize the death of our kids on the streets."

These were just a few of the many voices who showed up to be heard.

As I led the march through the streets of Chicago, I called out what these communities have been saying for years but have not had a platform to say loud enough. We demand safe streets. Enough is enough. Save our streets. The crowd echoed every word. Because they have lived it. Because they are tired of burying people they love while elected officials offer nothing but excuses.

National and local media were there because this story can no longer be ignored.

We started at Morgan Park High School, where Christian walked the halls before his life was stolen. As we marched through the streets of Chicago, I thought about what it means to return to the place where everything changed. The pain never goes away. But this weekend it was joined by something else. Hope. Because when you see a community come out and cheer for a march against the very violence that has devastated them, you understand that the people have not given up. They are not waiting to be saved. They are demanding to be heard. And it is past time for those in power to listen.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That leadership did not come from the governor's mansion this weekend. It did not come from City Hall. It came from the people who showed up, who linked arms, who said with their feet and their presence that they refuse to accept this as normal.

The Caldwell Foundation for Public Safety is not stopping here. We will continue to march in every city, in every state where our presence is needed most. The pain of losing a child to violence knows no zip code. Neither does our commitment to stopping it.

Governor Pritzker. Mayor Johnson. You had your chance to stand with these families. You chose not to, again and again. The people of Chicago are watching. And they deserve leaders who show up, not just at election time, but when it matters most.

item.title: States may defy DNC primary calendar as 'nobody is scared' of Ken Martin, CNN reporter says
item.description: CNN's Edward Isaac-Dovere said states like New Hampshire could defy the DNC primary calendar because "nobody" is scared of Ken Martin as chair.
item.content:encoded:
CNN's Edward Isaac-Dovere suggested Sunday that states could buck the DNC's primary schedule and hold its elections whenever they want to, pointing to New Hampshire specifically, and said that "nobody" is scared of DNC Chair Ken Martin.

"There is the possibility that a state could choose to not follow the DNC here and hold its primary when they want to," Dovere said as CNN host Manu Raju added that New Hampshire wanted to do this.

"And people saying, 'Hey, the DNC is broke. They can't do anything to help us anyway. Nobody is scared in any way of Ken Martin as the chair. And so maybe they'll just go and violate it.' It is not where the infrastructure of the party needs to be for going into 2026 and then 2028," Dovere added.

The DNC Rules and Bylaws Committee (RBC) panel, meeting in the nation's capital on Friday, picked South Carolina over Nevada to hold the party's first presidential nominating contest in 2028, a move that will likely maintain a key role in the primary calendar for Black voters, who are a crucial part of the Democrats' base.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

The decision came after intense lobbying by both states, and by New Hampshire and Iowa over the past year to hold the much-coveted lead-off Democratic primary in the race for the White House. 

The battle between South Carolina and Nevada was seen as a struggle between rewarding Black voters and outreach to Latino voters, with whom President Donald Trump and Republicans made major gains in the 2024 election, handing Democrats major setbacks.

The New Hampshire Democratic Party pointed Fox News Digital to a statement they put out on Friday, in which New Hampshire Democratic Party chair Ray Buckley said that the national party didn't learn anything from 2024.

"Today’s vote shows that many party insiders have learned nothing from 2024. New Hampshire has a proven track record of testing our candidates with a rigorous, fair, and efficient process, yet those qualities did not prevail. This committee’s vote does not change the realities governing New Hampshire’s primary, which are beyond the control of both this committee and our state party," Buckley said.

Buckley continued, "Democrats’ guiding North Star should be winning general elections, and New Hampshire Democrats will get back to work focusing on the 2026 elections and addressing the significant challenges facing America’s overwhelmed working class. Today’s vote moves the party further away from that objective."

SLOTKIN SAYS DEMOCRATIC PARTY NEEDS 'NEW LEADERSHIP': 'OLD MODELS ARE NO LONGER WORKING'

Raju asked if Martin would "survive" as chairman. Dovere said that the DNC chair could only be kicked out of the position if he resigned.

"He cannot be kicked out, and so it's up to him," he added. 

The DNC pointed Fox News Digital to a press release from June that highlighted the RBC's vote to strengthen penalties for states and candidates that buck the calendar.

The DNC voted at the end of June to strengthen penalties for states who participate in an unsanctioned contest in the early window of the presidential nominating calendar, according to a press release from late June.

The rules include implementing a $270,000 fine for any state that hosts an unsanctioned contest and increasing the delegates lost for states that host an unsanctioned contest from 50% to 100%, including all automatic delegates, among others. The penalties also prohibit any candidate's participation in DNC debates if they violate the early window rules.

DNC CHAIR KEN MARTIN THREW PHONE AT AIDE'S DESK, FACED HR COMPLAINT IN SIGN OF 'FRAYING NERVES': REPORT

Martin, while speaking to reporters on Friday, was asked how the DNC would respond, should states such as New Hampshire go rogue.

"We have put in significant penalties and sanctions, probably the most enforcement mechanisms ever, to make sure that, you know, folks know we are serious about making sure the calendar we put forth is abided by. Not just by the parties themselves – the state parties – but by also by the candidates," Martin told reporters.

He added, "If there’s a consequence to the candidates, right, the candidates are going to have to decide whether or not they want to lose all their delegates in the first four states. Whether they want to lose access to the debate stage. I can’t imagine if one of those states moves into the early window and is not sanctioned, that presidential candidates are going to risk it, risk going there."

New Hampshire state law requires that the state hold its primary election at least seven days before any other state holds a "similar" election.

When South Carolina was selected as the first primary state in 2024, New Hampshire defied the DNC, and former President Joe Biden left his name off the ballot, though he still won the state as a write-in.

While the DNC threatened to withhold New Hampshire's delegates in an effort to get the state to comply, they were ultimately restored in April 2024, ending the feud between the DNC and New Hampshire's Democratic Party in the previous presidential election cycle, according to the AP.

Martin faced a formal human resources complaint after allegedly throwing his phone at a junior aide's desk at the party's Washington headquarters in early July, The New York Times reported Sunday.

The Times cited six people familiar with the incident, none of whom witnessed it firsthand. Their accounts differed over how forcefully Martin threw the phone, but the newspaper reported that it landed on the aide's desk while Martin was reprimanding the staffer and led to a formal HR complaint.

NOTUS also reported on DNC turmoil on Sunday, noting a source briefed on the episode described it as worsening conduct.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"It's just f---ing unacceptable. This is spiraling behavior," the source told NOTUS.

The RNC blasted the national Democratic Party operation in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"The DNC is broke, leaderless, and imploding before America’s eyes. From states defying the national party to Ken Martin throwing his phone at staffers, it is undeniable that the inmates are running the asylum. While the Democrat Party collapses, Republicans are united, on offense, and focused on electing our candidates up and down the ballot this November," RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement.

item.title: Tennessee woman accused of turning traffic stop into a show for passing drivers by allegedly exposing herself
item.description: A seatbelt violation traffic stop in Lebanon, Tennessee, led to a K9 alert, alleged cocaine discovery, and a 66-year-old woman accused of exposure.
item.content:encoded:
What should have been a routine traffic stop in Lebanon, Tennessee last week turned into something of a spectacle, according to the Lebanon Police Department. A spectacle with a dog, alleged drugs and paraphernalia, and a woman accused of exposing herself.

Last Tuesday night, officers stopped a vehicle with a couple of senior citizens occupying it after they said they saw the passenger not wearing her seatbelt, reports WSMV. A K9 reportedly alerted officers to the possibility of drugs being in the vehicle.

After the 66-year-old passenger was taken out of the vehicle, she allegedly started exposing herself to passing drivers along the highway. A reason for the alleged impromptu show wasn't given.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Could it be a distraction technique on her part? Did she think that it would help her and the 68-year-old driver out somehow? Was it all strictly for the entertainment value?

It's anyone's guess, assuming, of course, that the allegations are true. This could have been a misinterpreted wardrobe malfunction. Those are commonplace in some parts of our society.

CALLING 911 BECAUSE A BAR WON’T SERVE YOU A JELL-O SHOT IS WHAT POLICE REFER TO AS A MISUSE OF SERVICES

Anyway, back to the investigation following that alert from the K9 to the possibility of narcotics being present in the vehicle. According to officers, they found what is believed to be cocaine and drug paraphernalia on both of the elderly occupants.

They were then both arrested. If the alleged exposure was meant to keep that from taking place, it didn’t work. They've both been charged with multiple offenses, according to the local outlet.

"Great work by K9 Donner and our D-Shift officers for their continued commitment to keeping our community safe," LPD said after the arrests.

Evidently it's just another Tuesday night in Lebanon, Tennessee. A traffic stop of a couple of senior citizens for a seatbelt violation ends in a couple of arrests with accusations of an elderly woman exposing herself.

item.title: Biden's Hur interview tapes could now go public after his attorneys wave white flag
item.description: Joe Biden's attorneys dropped their case blocking audio recordings from Robert Hur's classified documents probe, clearing way for congressional access.
item.content:encoded:
The months-long legal battle over the release of former President Joe Biden's recordings from interviews with his memoir ghostwriter — obtained during Special Counsel Robert Hur's classified documents investigation — came to an end on Monday.

Biden’s attorneys filed a motion last week to drop their case blocking the release of the audio recordings and transcripts after fighting to keep the material under wraps, noting that Biden is now a private citizen and is not seeking public office.

Obama-appointed Judge Tanya Chutkan of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia accepted the voluntary dismissal.

BIDEN’S FIGHT TO KEEP HUR INTERVIEW TAPES UNDER WRAPS SUFFERS FRESH COURT BLOW

The Justice Department obtained recordings of Biden's 2016 and 2017 conversations with Mark Zwonitzer, his ghostwriter for upcoming memoir "Promise Me, Dad." Hur’s team, meanwhile, prepared transcripts during its investigation into Biden’s handling of classified information.

Now, the Department of Justice can release the audio recordings and transcripts to the House Judiciary Committee after the Friday motion was accepted.

Hur investigated Biden’s handling of classified documents dating from his time as vice president in the Obama administration and as a U.S. Senator from Delaware. He declined to pursue criminal charges because he concluded prosecutors could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Biden willfully retained or disclosed the material.

He also said in shocking reasoning for the lack of prosecution that Biden could appear to a jury as a "sympathetic, well-meaning, elderly man with a poor memory" rather than an intentional violator of classified document laws.

HUNTER BIDEN RESURFACES IN LA, REACTS TO QUESTIONS ABOUT BIDEN TAPES, UFO FILES

The plaintiff, conservative think tank Heritage Foundation, has fought for more than two years to obtain the materials through FOIA requests, arguing that the public has an interest in reviewing the recordings and transcripts on which Hur based his decision.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Heritage Foundation for comment but did not hear back by time of publication.

A previous ruling favored Heritage after Biden’s attorneys filed an emergency request last week to block the release of the tapes.

"We conclude that any remaining incursion on personal privacy from disclosure of the now-redacted materials likely does not outweigh the public interest in disclosure," a divided three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit wrote in its ruling.

BIDEN SCORES TEMPORARY COURT VICTORY AS TRUMP-APPOINTED JUDGE DELAYS RELEASE OF HUR INVESTIGATION MATERIALS

Hur's report repeatedly referenced Biden's recorded conversations with Zwonitzer and described some exchanges as "painfully slow."

He said that Biden, at times, struggled to recall events and relay information, which further fueled scrutiny of Biden's cognitive abilities during a time when he was still running for reelection for president.

The Justice Department reversed its earlier position in February and said it intended to disclose redacted versions of the recordings and transcripts to the plaintiffs and the House Judiciary Committee.

Biden’s attorneys did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Debt-ridden Democrats tap a surprising asset as collateral for $15M loan
item.description: The Democratic National Committee used its headquarters as collateral for a record $15 million off-year loan as it carries $18.5 million in debt against the RNC's huge war chest.
item.content:encoded:
As the Democratic National Committee (DNC) shouldered significant debt and fell behind its GOP equivalent, Democratic leadership decided to use its headquarters as collateral for a $15 million loan, according to public records.

The loan, first reported by NOTUS news outlet, was taken out in 2025 as the DNC struggled to keep pace with the Republican National Committee’s fundraising efforts ahead of the midterm elections.

While taking out loans ahead of high-stakes races is common, and using property as collateral to do so is not unheard of, the line of credit secured by the DNC was the largest ever taken out by the committee for an off-year election, according to NOTUS. The terms of the loan allow the DNC to withdraw an additional $5 million beyond the $15 million it already has taken, public records show.

"This is not new," a DNC official told Fox News Digital Monday of the loan. "The loan documents were publicly released in November, and the DNC’s building was also used as collateral in our prior lines of credit in 2019, 2018, 2014 and many other years."

CASH-STRAPPED DNC SHELLED OUT MORE THAN $800K TO NON-VOTING TERRITORIES LIKE VIRGIN ISLANDS WHILE IN DEBT

What is new, however, is the DNC’s considerable debt.

The financial gap between Democrats and Republicans, as well as the former's higher-than-usual debt load, could leave the DNC with less flexibility to support candidates in the midterm elections. The national party’s debt and smaller cash reserves could limit its ability to respond quickly, invest broadly and compete with the GOP’s far larger war chest, a boon to conservatives who are currently struggling in the polls.

As of June 30, the DNC has $18.5 million in debt against just $16.3 million in cash on hand, according to campaign finance records. For comparison, the DNC ended 2022, the previous midterm cycle, with $30.5 million in cash against roughly $420,000 in debt.

The Republican National Committee, by comparison, had $128.5 million in cash with no debt as of June 30, per Federal Election Commission records.

That the DNC is using its headquarters as collateral for a loan isn't necessarily a sign that the organization is in its death throes. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, another major organization run by the party, used all of its assets as collateral for a $20 million line of credit in 2024, per a federal filing.

"Ken gaslighting us about the DNC’s finances and not being transparent about the financial situation makes us doubt if he can oversee the DNC during the most important primary of our lifetime," an anonymous DNC member told NOTUS.

The DNC’s heavy debt load has been accompanied by some cuts to spending.

For one, the DNC will not be making its traditional transfers to House and Senate campaign committees.

DNC CHAIR KEN MARTIN THREW PHONE AT AIDE'S DESK, FACED HR COMPLAINT IN SIGN OF 'FRAYING NERVES': REPORT

Over 2025 and into 2026, the RNC has consistently outraised the DNC and has maintained a much larger war chest. Other national Republican committees, such as the National Republican Senatorial Committee, have also raised more than their Democratic counterparts.

The financial outlook for Democrats isn’t all bleak. Individual Democratic candidates running in key elections, such as the Senate races in Georgia and Ohio, have raised significantly more money than Republican counterparts.

Amid its financial troubles, the DNC has made moves to tighten the lips of its leadership. Axios, citing two sources familiar, recently reported that the organization asked its leadership team to sign nondisclosure agreements ahead of a meeting about the party’s finances.

SUPREME COURT STRIKES DOWN LIMIT ON PARTY CAMPAIGN SPENDING IN COORDINATION WITH CANDIDATES

Decisions like that, however, have not stopped the leaks from coming out of the DNC.

One source told NOTUS that Democratic Party chair Ken Martin has had trouble convincing donors to make maximum donations, hamstringing efforts to raise large amounts of money. Other sources recently told The New York Times that Martin had a fit of rage in which he threw his phone at an aide’s desk.

"It pisses me off when I see leaks out of this building," Martin reportedly told staffers in May, according to the Times. "No more of that s–t. No more."

Despite the criticism, Martin remains publicly optimistic about the DNC’s finances.

"The current DNC has raised the most money of any DNC without the White House in the 198-year history of the Democratic Party," he wrote in a July 20 Substack article. "Through June 2026, this DNC reported total receipts of more than $207 million. During the comparable 18-month period of the last Trump-era cycle, when Democrats were also out of the White House and rebuilding toward a midterm election, the DNC reported $109 million."

Internally, however, some staff do no share Martin's assessment.

"They just have no money, and no clear path to either pay off their debt incurred by Ken," one source familiar with DNC fundraising told the Washington Post in April.

The New York Times recently reported that the DNC asked vendors it worked with no to send it bills until after Election Day, which the committee defended as standard practice. DNC leadership has also faced scrutiny for spending nearly $1 million in party work in U.S. territories, constituencies that will ultimately have no bearing on the outcome of the midterm elections, despite being strapped for cash.

item.title: Struggling Blue Jays send returning Max Scherzer to the mound against the surging Washington Nationals
item.description: Max Scherzer returns from the injured list for the Blue Jays against Washington, but his recent struggles on the mound raise serious concerns.
item.content:encoded:
We are just days away from the Major League Baseball trade deadline, so I would like to take this opportunity to remind everyone that it is a good time to reduce the bet size for a few days. This is the time of mid-game handshakes and hugs when players are traded away. That means your handicap can be thrown off significantly because guys are unavailable. Two teams who may be getting rid of guys face off today as the Blue Jays take on the Nationals.

The Toronto Blue Jays are 10 games under .500 for the season, and it is starting to look like last year's World Series runner-up might have no path to make the postseason. They have been bad on offense, but their pitching staff has been a problem as well. It just seems like nothing is going right for the team, and they are likely to start trading away anyone of interest to those looking to make a postseason push. It is a sad reality, and a follow-up to the progress they made last season.

There have been a number of issues on the mound for Toronto this season, including injuries. Max Scherzer is coming off of the injured list for this start. He was... not good on the hill this season. In May and June, he made five starts. Only one of those starts saw him complete more than four innings of work. He allowed two runs in six innings against the Diamondbacks, but then allowed 22 earned runs in 9.2 innings in the other four outings. Nationals hitters have done well against Scherzer in the past, going 10-for-34 against him.

ATHLETICS' SHEA LANGELIERS, TOP MLB TRADE DEADLINE TARGET, COULD BE OUT FOR SEASON AFTER DEVASTATING INJURY

The Washington Nationals have been surprising in a different way. This season, the team is 54-52, but they've been terrible at home. They are just 22-32 for the season when playing in Washington. The Nationals are in a strange spot because they are competitive in a year they weren't expected to be, and they have a lot of suitors if they choose to trade away pieces and continue with the planned rebuild. I'm not sure which direction they will go, but some offers might be too good to pass up.

Today, they send out Andrew Alvarez to the mound. He is 2-3 with a 4.22 ERA and a 1.50 WHIP. He has been slightly worse at home with almost a 5.00 ERA when on his home mound. His problem seems to be his walks more than anything else. He has issued 10 free passes in his last 16.2 innings. Couple that with the 16 hits, and it has led to 11 earned runs. The Blue Jays are second-to-last in walks this season, so maybe it won't be an issue. He has never faced Toronto before, though, so maybe they will be patient against him.

Part of me wonders how much left Scherzer has in the tank. He is 41 years old, so he is probably on his last leg of his Hall of Fame career. This would be a sad way for him to go out, but it doesn't look like he is going to dominate teams any longer. Maybe his return from injury will give him a bit better of a start.

JUSTIN VERLANDER ANNOUNCES HE WILL RETIRE AFTER THIS SEASON: 'I'VE REALIZED THAT TIME HAS COME'

I'm going to fade him and the Blue Jays, though. I think the Nationals are a better team with a fairly similar starter (at least at the moment). This is more of a coin flip than I normally like to play, but I think the looming deadline and Scherzer being unlikely to go deep into the game give the Nationals the edge in this one.

item.title: 'Allah commanded me': Three women stabbed in Paris, crowd subdues suspect
item.description: The Paris stabbing suspect uttered "it is Allah who commanded me" as a crowd pinned him down after three women were attacked at the brewery.
item.content:encoded:
The suspect subdued after allegedly stabbing three women in Paris on Monday uttered, "it is Allah who commanded me" to a crowd that appeared to be holding him down after the apparent terror attack.

The incident comes just days after another stabbing attack in England and a vehicular attack on a Pride parade in Berlin, Germany.

A 31-year-old man, whose name was not immediately released, was seen on the ground after allegedly stabbing three women, one of whom was reportedly pregnant.

WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS

French outlet "Le Figaro" reported his utterances translated to "it is Allah who commanded me" as police sources told the outlet the suspect has an "unbalanced" profile.

While many observers, including on X, immediately pointed to Islamic terrorism, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said he wanted to be "very careful about the motive for this violent act," pointing to the suspect’s "incoherent remarks."

Another translation of the exchange quotes one man as responding, "there is no Allah, bro," after the suspect allegedly attributed the stabbing to Allah, while another person says the crowd must "stampede this son of a b----."

AMERICAN TOURISTS STABBED OUTSIDE ATHENS' ACROPOLIS AS POLICE DETAIN SUSPECT IN APPARENT RANDOM ATTACK

"No, seriously, he’s crazy," a third person is quoted as saying in French.

"He stabbed my girl here," a woman says in French.

The suspect reportedly attacked women at the Two Domes brewery in the Porte de Clichy section of the French capital.

AT LEAST 1 DEAD, SEVERAL INJURED AFTER VAN RAMS INTO CROWD AT PRIDE FESTIVAL; SUSPECT 'KNOWN TO POLICE'

Two victims were listed in "absolute emergency" condition, while the third was listed in "relative emergency" condition, according to local press.

Reuters reported it had verified imagery of the suspect stabbing one woman while holding a knife in each hand.

The Paris-area attack comes two days after six men were arrested for "suspicion of murder" in connection with the stabbing of a 22-year-old man in Clapham, southwest London, United Kingdom, last week.

Metropolitan Police told the BBC the victim died after being stabbed at around 4:30 a.m. local time Saturday near Clapham High Street.

In Berlin, one person was pronounced dead and 29 were wounded after a suspect — later killed by German police — allegedly drove a vehicle into the public gathering.

The suspect in that case, Abdul Ballout, had German citizenship but "Lebanese roots," according to the Associated Press.

The outlet reported German officials are considering whether it was an act of Islamic extremism.

The cascade of violent incidents comes months after the White House released a National Security Strategy warning of "civilizational erasure" in Europe due to mass migration and demographic shifts, while highlighting a spate of terror attacks carried out by migrants.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The White House pointed to a range of European data to support the administration’s concerns, citing studies showing asylum migration costing the Netherlands €475,000 per migrant, illegal immigration costing France €1.8 billion in 2023 and non-Western migrants committing disproportionate shares of violent crime in Denmark and Germany.

The immigration status of the suspects in the three most recent attacks was not immediately confirmed.

Fox News Digital’s Michael Dorgan and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: McConnell out of hospital, still not 'medically cleared' to return to Senate
item.description: Mitch McConnell continues rehabilitation with multiple daily physical therapy sessions after his June fall, but childhood polio complicates his mobility.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., is out of the hospital and on the mend after suffering a fall last month, but he still isn’t "medically cleared" to return to the Senate.

His office on Monday released the latest update on the longtime Senate Republican, who has been absent from the upper chamber and the public eye for over a month. The Office of the Attending Physician said in a statement that McConnell "continues his recovery from a fall at home in June."

"OAP physicians visit with the senator every day, discussing all aspects of his rehabilitation care," the Office of the Attending Physician said. "Since his discharge from hospital care, he has maintained a strenuous course of physical therapy and rehabilitation, including multiple sessions a day designed to rebuild strength and reduce the risk of future falls."

TRUMP'S SAVE AMERICA ACT STALLS AS MCCONNELL'S ABSENCE COMPLICATES SENATE PATH

"His bout with childhood polio continues to be a significant factor in his mobility," they continued. "He is not yet medically cleared to leave the rehab facility and return to the office."

The latest update from McConnell-world comes after weeks of speculation and allegations that the longest-serving Republican leader in Senate history was dead or in a vegetative state. 

McConnell's extended absence from the Senate and murky timeline for his return come as Republicans are sprinting to clear the decks of several legislative priorities where his vote could be needed, including advancing a Russia sanctions package and confirming blockbuster nominees. 

MITCH MCCONNELL BREAKS SILENCE ON MYSTERY HOSPITALIZATION AFTER GRAHAM'S DEATH

The newest release included a photo of McConnell and his wife, former Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao, taken on Sunday, along with a statement from the lawmaker where he lamented that, because of his recovery, he would not be able to attend the annual barbecue at Fancy Farm, Kentucky, which has become a staple for him and politicians to speak in the Blue Grass State.  

"I’m still working hard to get back to my full schedule of work in the Senate and in Kentucky, keeping up with intense physical therapy per my doctors’ orders. Unfortunately, that means I won’t be able to make it to Fancy Farm, Kentucky this Saturday," McConnell said. 

MCCONNELL FACES FRESH CALLS TO COME CLEAN ABOUT HEALTH ISSUES

"There’s no place I’d rather be on the first Saturday in August than with the good people of western Kentucky, feasting on pork and mutton," he continued. "When I first attended forty-two years ago, Fancy Farm was a pretty lonely place to be a Republican. But, my, how times have changed. Today, western Kentucky is a conservative Republican sea of red. So I hate that I’ll miss the fun this year, but I’m sending my best wishes to the St. Jerome community for a successful picnic."

"As always, I appreciate all of your continued well wishes, and I’m looking forward to getting back to the Senate and to Kentucky soon."

His prolonged absence has prompted lawmakers in both chambers to call for more clarity and transparency about his condition and has led some to question the protocol for lawmakers going missing for months at a time. 

Rep. Tom Kean, R-N.J., just came back to the House after dealing with depression for months but kept the reasons tight-lipped until his return late last month. 

It also comes two weeks after the most recent official update from his office, which came the same day that the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's death was announced. It similarly included a photo of McConnell and Chao. 

His doctors noted in that update that McConnell had suffered a fall at home last month, but had not suffered fractures, broken bones, cardiac abnormalities, or a "stroke, tumor, or hemorrhage." However, early into his hospitalization he "developed pneumonia, which responded rapidly to antibiotic treatment."

item.title: Widow of soldier dad killed in Iraq delivers heartbreaking tribute after fatal drone mission
item.description: Mia Gonzalez-Swinton recalls the moment she learned Army Sgt. Michael Swinton was killed during a controlled demolition of an Iranian drone in Iraq.
item.content:encoded:
Army Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton's widow knew her life had changed forever the moment she saw two uniformed service members standing outside her front door.

"My stomach dropped," Mia Gonzalez-Swinton recalled Monday on "Fox & Friends First."

"I remember feeling sick almost... I felt like I was watching myself."

US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED IN IRAQ AS TROOPS RECOVER UNIDENTIFIED REMAINS IN JORDAN: CENTCOM

Swinton, 30, was killed while conducting a controlled demolition of a downed Iranian drone in Iraq, leaving behind his wife and their two young children, ages 6 and 4.

Recounting the moments after learning of his death, Gonzalez-Swinton said the loss still feels surreal as she and their children begin adjusting to life without him.

Asked how the children were coping, Gonzalez-Swinton said her daughter has started to understand that her father is gone, calling him her "angel," though she isn't sure how much either child fully comprehends.

TRAVELERS UNITE IN POWERFUL MOMENT OF SILENCE AS FALLEN US SERVICE MEMBER RETURNS HOME

Swinton's widow remembered him as a devoted father and husband who "loved his job," "loved this country," and cared deeply about everyone he met.

"Michael is an amazing man," she said. "He cared about anyone he crossed paths with. He loved his job. He loved this country."

Swinton, who will receive the Bronze Star, Purple Heart and Combat Action Badge, and be posthumously promoted to staff sergeant, had already received the Army Commendation Medal, Army Achievement Medal, Army Good Conduct Medal, National Defense Service Medal, Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal, Army Service Ribbon and Combat Action Badge.

Gonzalez-Swinton said she hopes people remember not only her husband's military service, but also the man he was away from the battlefield.

"I just want everyone to remember him, not only his Army awards and records, but the man he was," she said. "He loved his family, he cared for his friends, and I just don't want anybody to forget him."

Fox News' Eric Mac contributed to this report.

item.title: Your home is empty. Do burglars already know?
item.description: Burglary crews linked to Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce break-ins used public schedules and data brokers to target homes while owners traveled.
item.content:encoded:
In Argentina, authorities recently arrested three Chilean men wanted in the U.S. in connection with a South American theft group accused of burglarizing the homes of professional athletes.

Federal prosecutors linked the group to break-ins involving Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, Milwaukee Bucks player Bobby Portis and other athletes. Two of the suspects were also arrested in connection with a burglary at the home of tennis legend Juan Martín del Potro in Argentina.

According to prosecutors, the group identified targets through publicly available schedules and location information, then struck while athletes were away or playing games. Separately, the FBI has warned that international theft groups surveil homeowners to learn their routines and advises travelers to avoid announcing vacations on social media.

Online criminals can research your address, family, travel plans and estimated property value without ever driving down your street. Here's how criminals piece together those digital clues and what you can do to make your home harder to target.

It may be tempting to assume these crimes only affect people with mansions, expensive cars and celebrity lifestyles. Those cases make the news, but professional athletes and entertainers are far from the only targets. Security researchers and law enforcement agencies have tracked burglary crews using the same methods against everyday homeowners.

One recent case involved a Los Angeles content creator whose Silver Lake home was burglarized while she was traveling. Thieves reportedly took tens of thousands of dollars in designer goods. She had shared that she was away, which gave anyone watching her public account a useful clue.

For retirees, the risk can grow as travel becomes more frequent. You may finally take the cruise you have planned for years, spend a month in Florida each winter or take a road trip to visit your grandchildren. Those trips also create more opportunities to post "we made it" from an airport, beach or campground while your home sits empty.

Maybe you wait until you return home before posting vacation photos. However, someone in your life may share the information for you. A spouse might tag the airport. An adult child could post a picture of the grandchildren in front of your house. A neighbor might mention that you are away on your annual trip.

You have limited control over what other people share, so talk with your family before traveling. Ask everyone to wait until you return before posting locations, travel photos or details about how long you will be gone. Watching what your family posts helps, but social media provides only part of the information criminals can collect.

Investigators in Riverside, California, say they routinely find Zillow and Redfin searches on the phones of arrested burglary suspects. These sites may reveal an estimated property value, past sale prices and photos from an old listing. In some cases, criminals can view interior layouts, doors, windows and rooms before they approach the property.

Public property records can also reveal the owner's name, mailing address and purchase history. Meanwhile, data broker and people-search sites may connect that address with phone numbers, relatives, previous homes and other personal details. Combine "this person is traveling" with "this home has significant value," and criminals have the beginnings of a target list.

AI VOICE SCAMS CAN CLONE YOUR FAMILY’S VOICE

Search your name, phone number and home address to see what appears. You may find people-search profiles that list your age, relatives, address history and possible phone numbers. Real estate websites may still display old interior photos, even when you purchased the home years ago. Someone could use those details to connect your social media account with a specific property.

These steps can reduce the amount of useful information available to someone researching your home. They work best alongside basic home security measures, such as an alarm system, a doorbell camera, light timers and secure storage for valuables.

Save airport, hotel and sightseeing photos until you are back home. Real-time posts can tell strangers where you are and confirm that your house may be empty.

Tell your spouse, children, grandchildren and travel companions to wait before sharing your location or mentioning your travel dates.

Limit posts to people you know. Remove followers you do not recognize and check whether old public posts reveal your routines, vehicles or home address.

Ask a trusted neighbor to collect mail, newspapers and deliveries. You can also place a temporary hold on your mail before an extended trip.

Use timers or smart plugs to turn lights on and off at different times. Leaving every light off for two weeks can make an empty home easier to spot.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

Search your address on Zillow, Redfin and other real estate sites to see whether old listings reveal interior rooms, entrances or the layout of your home.

On Redfin, use a desktop browser and sign in. Select your name in the upper-right corner, choose My homes, select your claimed property and click Edit Photos. Check Hide listing photos, then select Yes, Hide Photos. This feature applies to off-market homes and currently does not appear in the Redfin mobile app.

On Zillow, sign in and select your profile icon, followed by Your Home. Choose your property and claim ownership if you have not already done so. From the Owner View, select Edit Facts. You can remove individual photos, delete all photos or check the option to hide photos from public view. Select Save Changes when finished.

Some off-market homes may not offer the editing option. In that case, submit a request to Zillow Customer Support. Other real estate sites may require you to claim the property, contact customer support or ask the original listing agent for help.

Data broker and people-search sites can connect your name, phone number, relatives and home address. Search for your information and request removal from sites that display it.

A data removal service can automate requests across hundreds of covered brokers and continue checking whether your information returns. It cannot erase government property records or every old real estate listing, so use it alongside the other home protection steps above.

You can also submit removal requests yourself, though the process may take more time and require repeat checks.

Search your name, address and phone number every few months. Look for new people-search profiles, outdated listings and social media posts that reveal more than you intended.

Burglary crews no longer need to spend days watching your street. Social media can reveal when you are away, while property records, real estate listings and people-search sites can reveal where you live and what your home may be worth. Retirement often brings more time for travel, which creates more opportunities for you or a family member to announce that your home is empty. You have limited control over public records and what your relatives post. However, you can delay travel posts, tighten privacy settings, remove old listing photos and reduce your exposure on data broker sites. Removing your personal information will never make you invisible. It can still make your home harder for online criminals to research and target.

item.title: Oregon ballot measure that would have criminalized hunting and fishing fails to qualify for vote
item.description: Oregon's IP28 ballot initiative fell roughly 13,000 voter signatures short, but the campaign to criminalize hunting and fishing isn't over yet.
item.content:encoded:
Oregon hunters, anglers and farmers can breathe a sigh of relief.

Initiative Petition 28 — the deceptively branded animal-rights proposal that would have effectively criminalized hunting, fishing, ranching and a long list of other normal activities — will not appear on Oregon’s November ballot after all.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

And this one came down to the wire.

Supporters of IP28 submitted more than 142,000 signatures, comfortably exceeding the 117,173 required to qualify for the ballot. But after two rounds of verification, the Oregon Secretary of State’s Office determined that only 104,262 of those signatures were valid.

That left the campaign roughly 13,000 signatures short.

Good.

Because while proponents called IP28 the People for the Elimination of Animal Cruelty Exemptions Act — or the warm and fuzzy-sounding "PEACE Act" — the proposal was never simply about prosecuting people who abuse animals. Oregon already has laws for that.

IP28 sought to remove the exemptions in Oregon’s animal-cruelty statutes that protect lawful hunting, fishing, trapping, ranching, farming, pest control and accepted animal-husbandry practices.

Under the proposal, killing or injuring an animal would have been classified as abuse unless it was necessary to prevent immediate harm to a person or another animal.

SPINY LOBSTER MINI SEASON KICKS OFF IN FLORIDA, DRAWING EAGER DIVERS TO THE WATER

That means hunters harvesting deer, anglers keeping fish, ranchers processing cattle, commercial fishermen bringing seafood to shore and farmers controlling pests could all have potentially faced criminal consequences.

The proposal was so extreme that opposing it became one of the few genuinely bipartisan causes left in American politics.

Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek, U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley, all 37 Democrats in the Oregon House and Republican lawmakers across the state spoke out against it. The Oregon Farm Bureau, Oregon Veterinary Medical Association and Oregon Hunters Association also opposed the initiative.

Kotek said Friday that she was "relieved" IP28 failed to qualify.

"I know from conversations with Oregonians across the state that this measure would have done nothing to help them," she said.

She’s right.

IP28 would not have created some peaceful wildlife paradise where every deer, elk, fish, cow and invasive pest lived happily ever after. It would have undermined the very wildlife-management system that keeps animal populations and habitats healthy.

Hunters and anglers provide enormous amounts of conservation funding through license sales and federal excise taxes on firearms, ammunition, archery equipment and fishing gear. Those dollars help states acquire habitat, maintain boat ramps, conduct wildlife research, restore species and operate public recreation programs used by everyone.

Travis Thompson, a conservation advocate who helped lead the successful effort to establish a constitutional right to hunt and fish in Florida, recently explained to OutKick Outdoors that sportsmen’s contributions support far more than hunting and fishing.

"It’s used to acquire lands. It’s used for boat-ramp maintenance. It’s used for youth programs. It’s used for all sorts of things that everyone benefits from," Thompson said. "The places where I hunt aren’t just limited to me hunting. There are people who bike on them, ride horses, walk their dogs, hike or bird-watch."

Watch Travis Thompson's full interview with OutKick Outdoors here:

Eliminating hunting and fishing would not eliminate the need for wildlife management, either. It would simply transfer the cost from sportsmen to taxpayers — assuming the state continued managing wildlife at all.

Without regulated hunting, growing wildlife populations can lead to habitat destruction, disease, starvation, crop damage and more vehicle collisions. Invasive species would create another obvious problem, since IP28 did not include a broad exemption allowing them to be removed before they devastated native ecosystems.

As Thompson put it, wildlife policy must be driven by science rather than "emotions or feelings."

That is exactly why the defeat of IP28 matters beyond Oregon.

Across the country, hunters, anglers and conservation groups are fighting two related battles. In some states, activists are attempting to restrict hunting, fishing, trapping, the use of live bait and other traditional outdoor activities. In others, sportsmen are trying to pass constitutional protections recognizing the right to hunt and fish.

Florida became the 24th state to adopt such a protection when voters approved Amendment 2 in 2024 with 67.4% support. Thompson and the International Order of Theodore Roosevelt (IOTR) are now working with lawmakers and advocates in states including Ohio, Colorado, Delaware and New Hampshire.

The point of those amendments is not to create a free-for-all or override wildlife regulations. States would still manage seasons, bag limits and conservation policy using science.

Instead, they create a higher legal threshold for activists seeking to eliminate hunting and fishing altogether.

"We know that anti-hunters are coming," Thompson said. "What we want is to ensure that when they get here, we’ve got a backstop."

IP28 is a perfect example of why that backstop could become important.

Four years ago, Thompson noted, many people dismissed an earlier version of the Oregon proposal because they didn't believe it would ever reach the ballot. It was too extreme. This year, the campaign came close enough to submit more than 142,000 signatures.

The fact that approximately 38,000 of those signatures were ultimately rejected is worth celebrating. But it would be foolish to assume the campaign is dead.

This was chief petitioner David Michelson’s third failed attempt to place the issue before Oregon voters. And he has made it clear that supporters view this as a long-term campaign, not a one-election project.

"We know that this is unlikely to pass in 2026," Michelson said in a previous interview. "No one on the campaign thinks that this will pass right now."

Instead, Michelson said the goal was to create an organization capable of pursuing similar initiatives in Oregon "in multiple election cycles in a row" and eventually launching them in other states.

That should get everyone’s attention.

Getting it onto the ballot would have helped IP28 supporters to collect voter data, build a donor base, normalize the proposal and identify language capable of attracting broader support next time.

They failed.

That is unquestionably good news for Oregon’s hunters, anglers, farmers, ranchers, wildlife professionals and consumers.

But they also got close — much closer than during previous attempts.

So enjoy the win, but keep paying attention.

Because IP28 will not be on the ballot this November, but the larger effort to eliminate hunting and fishing rights is not going anywhere. And neither can the people determined to protect them.

Love all things hunting, fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick Outdoors on Instagram and TikTok!

item.title: Trump critic Massie joins Democrats in unprecedented bid to sue White House over Iran war
item.description: Thomas Massie accused President Trump and Secretary Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, joining Democrats in a resolution to sue over the Iran war.
item.content:encoded:
A lone House Republican is joining Democrats in an effort to get President Donald Trump sued over the Iran war.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., is one of the co-sponsors of a new resolution aimed at compelling House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., to sue the Trump administration over allegations the president is violating federal law with the U.S. conflict in the Middle East.

The bill is also being led by Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, as well as Reps. Jim McGovern, D-Mass., Gabe Amo, D-R.I., Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., Jason Crow, D-Colo., and Ro Khanna, D-Calif.

Massie accused Trump and Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth of being "in blatant violation of two sections of the War Powers Resolution of 1973."

TRUMP AIMS TO RESET WAR POWERS CLOCK WITH CONTROVERSIAL BID TO BYPASS CONGRESS

"For the first time since the law was enacted, a concurrent resolution has passed in accordance with 5(c) of the law, but the White House has ignored it. It seems they’ve assumed the law is unconstitutional, but no court has ever found that to be the case, so the law remains on the books while the White House flouts it. In the 1983 case INS v. Chadha, the Supreme Court did not opine on the 1973 War Powers Resolution. It’s time for the courts to settle this, and that’s what our legislation directs," Massie said.

"They’ve also violated section 5(b) of the law, but rather than ignore the law, they’ve perpetuated a ruse that the 60-day limit on Presidential military activity does not apply with respect to the Iran war, because each time they effect a temporary ceasefire, the statutory clock restarts. We believe no court would agree with this absurdity, and this should be litigated as well."

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE ED GALLREIN CALLS KENTUCKY WIN A ‘DAVID VS. GOLIATH’ VICTORY AFTER DEFEATING MASSIE

Massie was one of four House Republicans who voted with Democrats to rebuke Trump over the Iran war with a war powers resolution that passed last week. The resolution is largely symbolic, however, and has no practical effect.

His open criticism of Trump also earned Massie a primary challenger backed by the president, who wound up defeating the sitting congressman and will likely take his place in the House of Representatives next year.

But the new resolution to sue Trump over the Iran war is not likely to get a full House vote unless Massie or Democrats use maneuvers to force it over the objections of House GOP leaders.

REP TOM BARRETT: IT’S UP TO CONGRESS TO PREVENT ANOTHER ENDLESS AMERICAN WAR

In his comments to Fox News Digital, Massie also criticized congressional leadership for not doing more to block the war.

"Unfortunately, Speaker Johnson has chosen to let the power of our institution atrophy and is doing harm to our constitutional authority by his inaction motivated by political expediency," Massie said. "Although both Iraq wars and the war in Afghanistan were authorized by AUMFs [Authorization for Use of Military Force] from Congress, the Trump administration has sought no such Congressional authorization for the war in Iran, and is therefore operating unconstitutionally."

Johnson, for his part, told reporters last week that he did not believe an AUMF was necessary but suggested he wanted to see an end to the war.

"The administration is working very hard. The commander in chief and the whole Department of War, they're working very hard to bring this to a resolution. There's a lot of discussions about how that will be done," Johnson told reporters Tuesday. "We're all closely watching those developments. Of course, I don't think an AUMF is in order right now. I think we need to bring this to a resolution."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

The No. 2 leader in the House of Representatives is hammering Democrats after a slate of far-left primary victories ahead of the November midterms, warning a "civil war" is in store for their party.

"There's like this Bolshevik revolution that has taken over the Democrat Party. It's scary to see because many of them are espousing communist viewpoints — very, very radical viewpoints — and they're winning. They're beating liberals," Scalise told Fox News Digital in an interview.

Republicans are seizing on wins by candidates affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) as proof that Democrats as a whole are shifting further left than where most American voters are.

FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS

"This is surely not your father's Democrat Party," Scalise said. "There's never been a sharper contrast between Republicans who believe in freedom and individual opportunity and Democrats who are moving toward socialism."

It comes after several DSA-linked candidates toppled incumbent progressive Democrats in recent weeks.

Reps. Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., and Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., both lost primaries to candidates backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, himself a DSA member. Goldman's challenger Brad Lander, however, left the DSA after the Oct. 7, 2023, attack in Israel.

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST WINS IN NEW YORK EXPOSE GROWING RIFT BETWEEN DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT, INSURGENT LEFT

Another DSA-backed candidate in Denver toppled longtime Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo.

Those victories in safe blue seats mean all three will have a glide path to the House of Representatives come November.

"The liberals in the Democrat Party are being beaten in primaries by socialists and that's foreboding for kind of this civil war that's going on in the Democrat Party," Scalise said. "I think if you go through most of middle America, and I go there a lot, all of those districts, they don't want socialism — and yet that's what's on the ballot."

Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) Chair Rep. Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., leader of House Democrats' campaign arm, told Fox News Digital in response that her party was focused on lowering costs and panned the GOP criticism as "desperate."

"The midterms will ultimately be a referendum on who is going to lower costs and help improve the lives of everyday Americans — which House Republicans have failed spectacularly to do. In the purple, majority-making districts — Democratic candidates are running substantive campaigns focused on lowering costs, saving health care, and fighting to make life affordable for working families," DelBene said. "Republicans already know they’ve lost the American people, and that’s why they are resorting to desperate attacks that aren’t actually about the pocketbook issues, but just baseless spin that falls flat with voters who are eager to reject Republicans."

Republicans are facing an uphill battle to keep control of the House in November, given historic trends that show the president's party traditionally faces significant losses halfway through the White House term.

But GOP leaders are hopeful that they can reverse that as lawmakers get ready to spend the entire month of August in their home districts making their case to Americans.

item.title: Waltz slams France after stunning social media attack on US after UN vote
item.description: France accused the U.S. of standing alongside North Korea and Russia after a contentious U.N. vote to reappoint Volker Türk as human rights chief.
item.content:encoded:
France’s mission to the United Nations in Geneva launched a verbal attack against the U.S. following a contentious vote to give U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk another four-year term, accusing Washington of abandoning its role as a global human rights leader.

"The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore," the official French mission account posted on X Saturday. "Today, it stands alongside North Korea, Nicaragua, Mali & Russia, isolated. And the world no longer listens to it."

The mission added the hashtag "#AmericaAlone."

IRAN SECURES UN ROLE WITH BACKING FROM UK, FRANCE, CANADA, AUSTRALIA AS US STANDS ALONE

U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz fired back, accusing France of using the attack to distract from its support for Türk.

"It is disappointing — though not surprising — that this is how France deflects on its shameful vote to coddle some of the worst human rights abusers," Waltz wrote on X. "France voted for someone who has been lecturing free, sovereign democracies like the United States, the UK, and Israel, while cozying up to the world’s worst oppressors."

During the vote by Ambassador Jeff Bartos, the U.S. representative for U.N. management and reform, declared that the U.N. human rights system "has been losing credibility for decades."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM

"Mr. Türk has guided it to its deathbed," Bartos said. "And if you vote to reappoint Volker Türk for a four-year term, it will kick the bucket."

Bartos accused Türk of disproportionately condemning democracies while failing to respond adequately to abuses committed by authoritarian governments.

He said Türk had criticized the United States, Britain, France, Australia, Italy and, more than any other country, Israel. Bartos also accused Türk of remaining silent for 12 days after the Iranian government allegedly began a new wave of violence against its citizens, while quickly condemning U.S. military action against Iran.

Bartos further criticized Türk’s office for calling on Washington to lift sanctions on Cuba, maintaining what he called a discriminatory database targeting American companies and enabling the U.N.’s "anti-Israel machinery."

ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES

France’s U.N. Ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont offered a sharply different assessment during the General Assembly debate, saying Türk had demonstrated "rigor and impartiality" during a first term marked by growing attacks on multilateral institutions and the universality of human rights.

"He has been a voice of conscience, confronting states with reality and their responsibilities," Bonnafont said.

An official familiar with the U.S. position told Fox News Digital on background that American officials were surprised by France’s "brazen" public attack and rejected the suggestion that opposing one U.N. official’s reappointment amounted to opposing human rights.

The official said Washington and other delegations were also caught off guard by the expedited vote because Türk’s current term does not expire until Oct. 11.

The United States sought to postpone consideration for one week to allow additional consultations, but member states rejected the request. The General Assembly then approved Türk’s reappointment by a vote of 144-10, with 13 abstentions, extending his tenure from Oct. 12, 2026, through Oct. 11, 2030.

The assembly also rejected a Russian proposal to extend Türk’s term only through the end of 2026, which would have allowed the next U.N. secretary-general to participate in selecting the human rights chief.

WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

France’s post grouped Washington with authoritarian governments that also opposed Türk, but did not address whether those countries voted against his reappointment for the same reasons. The U.S. said its opposition reflected both concerns about Türk’s record and objections to the accelerated process.

UN Watch, a Geneva-based watchdog, published a 2024 analysis of public statements initiated by Türk or his office between Oct. 17, 2022, and Oct. 31, 2024.

The organization concluded that Türk criticized the United States more frequently than China, North Korea, Cuba, Saudi Arabia and Qatar combined. It also said it found no self-initiated criticism during that period concerning abuses by Cuba, North Korea, Algeria, Eritrea, Mauritania, Lebanon or Qatar.

UN Watch’s methodology excluded statements required by the Human Rights Council, comments in mandated reports, broad updates to the council and other remarks that were not initiated at Türk’s discretion. Its findings therefore do not encompass every country reference, report or action by Türk’s office.

UN Watch Executive Director Hillel Neuer called the renewal "rushed and unprecedented" and said it was "unseemly" for French President Emmanuel Macron’s government to attack the United States while celebrating Türk’s reappointment.

Nile Gardiner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, responded more bluntly.

"Perhaps show some gratitude instead?" Gardiner wrote on X. "The French owe their very existence as a sovereign nation to The United States."

Türk’s supporters argue that his willingness to criticize powerful democracies is part of his responsibility to apply human rights standards universally. France and the European Union maintained that he had performed his duties objectively and that Secretary-General António Guterres acted within the rules allowing a high commissioner to serve a second four-year term.

Türk is set to become the first U.N. human rights chief to serve two complete four-year terms since the position was established in 1993.

item.title: Eric Bieniemy son jailed for shooting his mother while Kansas City Chiefs coach is away at training camp

item.title: Trump admin targets woke schools accused of hiding students' gender transitions from parents
item.description: Linda McMahon says the Education Department and DOJ are taking action against two school districts accused of hiding students' gender transitions.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The Department of Education is taking enforcement actions on National Parents' Day against two school districts accused of hiding students' gender transitions from parents — a move that could now could cost them federal funding.

The action reinforces President Donald Trump's campaign against radical left-wing gender ideology and the push for more parental rights in the classroom.

"As a mother and a grandmother, it is unconscionable that any school district would hide the most sensitive information about children in their care from their own parents. This is not only an affront to basic moral principles, but also to parents’ rights under federal law," Secretary of Education (ED) Linda McMahon exclusively told Fox News Digital.

VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

"Today, ED and DOJ are putting districts on notice that we will use every tool available to hold them to account for this egregious behavior," McMahon added. "Under the Trump Administration, ED and DOJ are working together to vigorously uphold parents’ federal protections, and we will work to ensure that no parent is ever kept in the dark about important matters relating to their children."

The Education Department is working with the Department of Justice to investigate Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) violations against Anne Arundel County Public Schools in Maryland and Ann Arbor Public Schools in Michigan. The investigations concern allegations that the districts hid information from parents about their own children's health and wellbeing, and could result in federal funding being withheld from the schools, Fox News Digital has learned.

FERPA is a federal law that gives parents the right to see their child's school records, ask for mistakes to be corrected and generally control who can access that information about their child.

The Trump administration is looking into whether the schools violated FERPA.

LOUDOUN COUNTY PARENTS NOT 'SATISFIED' AFTER SCHOOL OFFICIALS TESTIFY ON TRANSGENDER POLICIES

One case the administration is investigating involves a Maryland family who says they were blindsided after discovering school staff presented their daughter as male during the school day without their knowledge or consent. The parents only learned what was happening after receiving an email that referred to their daughter using male pronouns.

According to the Education Department, school administrators refused to provide the parents with additional information, with the assistant principal declining to turn over records related to their child's gender transition.

The department is also looking into a policy at Ann Arbor Public Schools that allows teachers to help students hide their "transgender status" from parents.

The school district has a policy that directs school officials to maintain records related to a "gender identity" in a separate filing system.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

Ann Arbor Public Schools must justify their policy to the Education Department by Aug. 11, 2026 or else risk losing its federal funding.

Fox News Digital reached out to the school districts in Maryland and Michigan for comment but did not hear back at time of publication.

item.title: Arizona Diamondbacks vs Pittsburgh Pirates betting preview with trade deadline decisions looming
item.description: Merrill Kelly faces Mitch Keller as the Arizona Diamondbacks visit the Pittsburgh Pirates, with both teams on the trade deadline bubble today.
item.content:encoded:
We had just one play on the diamond last night, and it was a no-sweat win, just how we like them. The Phillies trounced the Yankees, and it happened pretty early in the game, so we were able to coast to victory. I am hoping this is the same situation today, but I'm guessing my play for today's game will not come as easily. Let's break down this game between the Diamondbacks and Pirates.

I've been reading a lot right now about the trade deadline and what could potentially happen. Most of it never comes to fruition, but it is still fun to explore what analysts think will happen. One of the teams that is on the bubble of being a buyer and a seller is the Arizona Diamondbacks. There has been a rumor for about a year about them trading Ketel Marte, but this team is also 55-51 for the year. They could add a bat and make a splash for their offense, much like they did a couple of years ago.

Last year they were sellers, and they traded away one of their mainstays in the rotation, Merrill Kelly. He toes the rubber tonight for the Diamondbacks. For the year, Kelly is 8-8 with a 5.12 ERA and a 1.48 WHIP, not exactly numbers that will lead to a major return should they try to flip him again. He has been slightly better on the road with a 4.28 ERA. He also has been solid in July, putting together his best month of the season. He has thrown 22 innings and allowed just six earned runs. Most of his problem has been the home run ball because he has allowed one in each start this month. Overall, the Pirates are just 5-for-25 against Kelly.

ATHLETICS' SHEA LANGELIERS, TOP MLB TRADE DEADLINE TARGET, COULD BE OUT FOR SEASON AFTER DEVASTATING INJURY

The Pittsburgh Pirates are another fairly interesting team for this year's deadline. They are unlikely to be heavily involved in the trade market. I doubt they will be sellers, and they may not have the means to be major buyers. They are slightly above .500 with a 52-50 record, so trading away players when they have a shot at the postseason seems unlikely. They've been one of the better-hitting teams in the sport, so I don't know that it helps to trade for another bat, but maybe the pitching staff can get an upgrade.

Perhaps they can get today's starter, Mitch Keller, to improve his performance. For the season, Keller is 6-7 with a 4.90 ERA and a 1.31 WHIP. He has been very bad in Pittsburgh this season, with a 5.68 ERA at home. He also has allowed 26 earned runs in his last 40 innings. He has allowed at least three earned runs in each of his past six starts at home. He is coming off one of his best starts of the year, a road outing, going five scoreless innings and allowing just three hits. Diamondback hitters are batting .202 against Keller.

The numbers don't really scream any true success for either of these lineups against the opposing starter. There are some guys who have performed well, but no one that makes me think this will be a super high-scoring game. I also don't think I can advocate for the under given how these pitchers have performed this season.

I'm going to take the Diamondbacks in this one. Keller has been bad at home this season, and Kelly hasn't been great, but has at least been better on the road. There is some sharp action coming in on Arizona as well, with the line moving in their favor. I'm going to back the Diamondbacks on the moneyline, but just know this might be a bit sweaty.
